hyps.why: Turning a missing direct 0->3 edge into a conv adds a new input-to-output path (about +66 to +78 points in the sparse parents, up to +11 in dense ones), while replacing an existing op changes little.
Adding a skip where edge 3 was absent restores a direct path and gains more (+2.8/+3.9/+16.5 in the clean 3x3 parent) than swapping an existing op for skip (+0.6/+1.8/+5.2).
Replacing a skip with a conv on edge 3 lost accuracy on all three datasets (-0.6/-1.8/-5.2), unlike the gains seen when edge 3 was none.
With the direct 0->3 edge missing, removing edge 0 cuts the remaining input paths and gave the largest drop (-3.4/-5.1/-6.8).
When edge 3 is absent, a skip on edge 5 gives a cheap path to the output and helped on all three datasets (+3.6/+4.9/+14.3), while it is neutral or negative with edge 3 present.
Replacing avg_pool on edge 5 with a conv gave consistent gains (+1.4/+1.1/+4.4), larger than when replacing a 1x1 conv.
Re-enabling a missing edge 5 with a conv helps on all datasets (+0.5/+1.5/+3.0), more than upgrading a 1x1 conv.
With edge 1 removed, the direct 0->3 path matters more, so a skip on edge 3 gains more (+0.8/+3.1/+6.9 vs +0.6/+1.8/+5.2).
With edge 2 removed, there are fewer alternative routes to the output, so a skip on edge 3 helps more (+0.8/+2.0/+5.9).
Replacing an existing avg_pool on edge 3 with a conv gives roughly zero or negative change, far below the gain from filling an empty edge 3.
